newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Coffee seen consolidating before new rise.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Coffee seen consolidating before new rise.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Coffee looks set to consolidate, before heading for new peaks, technical analysts said.
London traders called it to open unchanged on Thursday. Asian traders' ideas were around the same level, but any piece of news could spark an explosive rally in the market, they said.

"I suspect it may consolidate for the short term," independent technical analyst Elli Gifford said. In the slightly longer term she put $1,900 as a psychological target, with $1,930 as the next real resistance.
In the longer term coffee could go higher and take a look at $2,000, she said.
"It's forming a base," Gifford said. "If the base is a real one, it could go a lot higher."
"It's overbought, but I don't think that matters a jot," she said.
Jorge Cardenas, head of Colombia's powerful National Coffee Growers' Federation said that the country will have "enormous difficulties" meeting export schedules.
He blamed the situation on supply worries caused by a best-case forecast of a 10.2 million 60-kg bag crop for the 1996/97 coffee year -- compared to 12.9 million bags last year.

Smaller than expected crops in many Latin American countries -- most notably second-largest producer Colombia, the onset of winter in Brazil and low inventory levels in consumer countries have all contributed to fuel a five-month upswing in coffee futures.
